title: A Barracuda Hits 36 mph and Attacks Anything That Glints

scenes.text: Divers here take off their watches first.
Below them: the great barracuda. Up to two metres, with needle teeth that slot into holes in the opposite jaw.
It hangs still, then goes from zero to 36 miles an hour in seconds. It rams a fish and chops it in half.
The trigger is a glint. To a barracuda, a flash of metal looks like the silver flank of a fish.
Attacks on people are rare, but a dive knife, a watch or a ring can draw a strike. One diver took 31 stitches.
Two deaths have been blamed on them, in 1947 and 1957. So the watch comes off. The barracuda is still watching.

description:
The great barracuda can reach two metres, accelerates from zero to 36 mph in seconds, and attacks shiny objects it mistakes for the glint of a fish, which is why divers are told to leave jewellery and shiny gear behind.
Attacks on humans are rare and usually involve spearfishing or a shiny object; a 1960 diver in Florida needed 31 stitches, and deaths were attributed to barracuda in 1947 and 1957.
Would you swim with one?

first_comment: Barracuda are ram-biters: they hit at full speed and slice a fish in two. What's the scariest thing you've seen while diving?
